why: The terrain and climate laws read seven numbers the atlas names but does not quantify: the continental wavelength, the relief, the sea line, the datum, the equatorial base temperature and the two ridge terms. They are authored in `display-packages/worldgen/package.shspec` and `voxel_shapers::worldgen` reads them into the `Config` every `WorldSpec` is built from, so the world's depth and its continents' wavelength are a package row rather than a literal in `spec.rs`. The game mounts that folder at boot and prints the constants and the spawn column's elevation, so a row edited on disk changes the ground the same binary draws. The rows below are the package's seven constants, in the package's order, and `worldgen::tests::the_record_names_the_packages_rows` fails if this record and the mounted package disagree on a knob, its value or its unit. The measured rows after them are the elevation the default world reads at two fixed columns and its land fraction over a 4 x 4 km grid, reproduced by `cargo run -p voxel-shapers --example worldgen-probe`.
recipe: cargo run -p voxel-shapers --example worldgen-probe (Config::default() read from display-packages/worldgen/package.shspec, seed 2468, tick 0; elevation from `terrain::elevation_m` at the two columns the far-terrain module already measures, and the land fraction over 4 096 columns of 64 m from -2 048 m to +2 048 m; the doctored rows are the same spec with `relief_m` doubled)
measured: 2026-10-28, the pass that made the world's constants a mounted package

rows.name: continental wavelength
rows.note: continental §2 (Continentalness: from maritime margins to inland climates). One continental cycle at the 1/8 scale; `continent_frequency` is its reciprocal, 0.0025 per engine metre.

rows.name: relief
rows.note: terrain §3 (terrain is a climate modifier: elevation, slope, aspect, relief) and §7 (mountains: relief changes rainfall, exposure, snow distribution and erosion). The peak-to-trough amplitude the elevation law can reach.

rows.name: sea line
rows.note: continental §2: the ocean is the maritime end of continentalness. A column whose regional elevation is below this line is sea; the flat band in the 60 m frame is this surface, not a plane quad.

rows.name: datum
rows.note: terrain §3 (elevation is the first terrain variable). The datum the whole surface is measured from, and the term the continental field is added to.

rows.name: base temperature
rows.note: continental §1 (the climate engine: heat, water, seasonality) and terrain §1 (the first filter: energy and water). The equatorial sea-level annual mean the latitude penalty is measured down from; the shipped 45 deg world reads about +8 C.

rows.name: ridge frequency scale
rows.note: continental §3 (mountains reorganize climate over short horizontal distances). The ridged term runs at six continental frequencies, so a range's wavelength is 1/400 x 1/6 = 66.7 engine metres — `terrain::range_wavelength_m`.

rows.name: ridge amplitude
rows.note: continental §3 and terrain §7. How much of the relief the ridged term raises where plates converge; gated by the tectonic term, so a stable plate raises nothing.

rows.name: elevation at (0.5, -100.5)
rows.note: The column the far-terrain module measures its flat band at: sea, 2.2 m below the 16 m line. Doubling `relief_m` on disk reads 11.56 m here.

rows.name: elevation at (0.5, -1000.5)
rows.note: The shore column: essentially the sea line, which is why the eye 60 m above it sees water underfoot. Doubling `relief_m` reads 16.06 m.

rows.name: land fraction over 4 x 4 km
rows.note: 1 831 of 4 096 columns above sea level at 64 m spacing. A world with a sea and a shore, not the land fraction of 1.00 the old (sea 0, datum 64, relief 140) default produced.

rows.name: the built game reads a doctored relief row
rows.note: With `GEN-0002`'s value edited from 40 to 80 on disk and no rebuild, the boot line read `relief 80 m ... stands at 11.56 m` at the spawn column instead of 13.78 m; restoring the file read 13.78 m again. The same run is the package mount's evidence.

unstable.name: the sea line's exact reading at a shoreline
unstable.note: The elevation at (0.5, -1000.5) is within 3 cm of the sea line, so the fifth decimal is not a stable row; the 1 % window is chosen for that and the value is recorded as a note rather than a law.
